feature: Animated charts you can drop into a video
summary: A video's Library has an Animated Charts chip with six charts (bars, horizontal bars, line, donut, big number, comparison) that build in like a title: bars grow one after another as their numbers count, lines draw, donuts sweep. Their numbers are typed or pasted into a Chart section.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Open any recording; walk: Scripts/playtest/animated-charts-walk.json.

try.do: View > Library, press Catalog, then the Animated Charts chip.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Double click Bar Chart: it lands at the playhead on a Title track, picked, with the Chart section in the panel.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Copy four rows from a spreadsheet (a label and a number each) and press the clipboard button beside Data.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Home and Space: the bars grow in one after another while each value counts up.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Set Unit to $ Dollars, then Kind to Horizontal Bars.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: In the Title section pick another Theme and Font Pair, and Background None to lay the chart over the recording.
Open the chart's row on the timeline and drag a Bar's part bar to retime when it grows.
Watch every chart in the reel: queue/audits/2026-10-17-chart-reel-contact.png and the chart-reel MP4s.

evaluate: Do the bars, line and donut build in a way you would use in a product video, or do they want more motion?
Is pasting rows from a spreadsheet with one button the way you expect to get numbers in?
Does a chart over your recording (Background None) read clearly enough?
Is Kind in the Chart section enough to switch between bar, line and donut, or should each be its own thing?
Is the big number's count-up speed right, or should it land faster?
rough: No mock draws a chart or the Chart section (video-library.html only names the Animated Charts chip), so its rows are the panel's own controls under UX-PATTERNS §4.
Whether the look and build are right is your call on the reel: decision animated-charts-you-can-drop-into-a-video-do-the-six-charts-build-in-and-l.
Changing the data or the theme lays the chart's pieces out again: a key or an effect set by hand on one bar is lost (the pieces keep their ids, and a part's retimed in and out are kept).
Negative values draw as a flat bar on the baseline; the line chart's axis starts at nought, so small changes look flat.
A row wearing the theme's colour shows a struck-through swatch in its colour well, which can read as no colour at all.
Count Up is new in the Part section's In menu, offered only for words; any title's number can now count up.
With a crowded dock the Library shelf's second row could not be scrolled into view by a walk: filed as find-out-whether-a-crowded-dock-can-hide-the-lib.
Every picture here was taken with the window behind another app (shotNote says what that changes).
